output.headline: Same-sub-sector strategic with five closed deals and a Midwest precedent; ranked first on the priority list and able to support upper-quartile pricing.
output.differentiator: Five deals in the target's own sub-sector, more than any other buyer on the priority list, all closed; its median multiple paid sits above the comparable-deal median. [T:record, K:closed_share, V:comps]
output.why_them: Own-sub-sector strategic; pays above the comparable median

acquirer_overview.title: Nonprofit system formed by merger, with five closed deals
points: Nonprofit system headquartered in Charlotte, NC, created when Advocate Aurora Health and Atrium Health merged; 69 hospitals (2024). [P:1, P:2, P:3]
Five deals, 2016 to 2023: all closed, all control, all in the target's sub-sector, none in adjacent provider sub-sectors. [T:record, K:closed_share, K:control_share]
Median deal $436M, ranging from $35M to $2,022M; 2 deals since 2022. [T:record, K:recent]

strategic_fit_thesis.title: Sub-sector focus is the strongest factor, backed by platform-build history
points: Share of deals in the target's sub-sector is the strongest factor; target margin close to what it usually buys is a strong one. [S:sector_share, S:margin_fit]
Platform Build in 2 of 5 deals and Scale in 2 of 5, motives that fit a target of this kind. [M:platform_build, M:scale]
Has bought from this kind of seller (a modest factor); its regional history is a slight factor against. [S:own_fit_s, S:geo_fit]

precedent_activity.title: Precedents run from $35M to $2,022M at 9.3x to 18.5x
points: Charter Care Partners ($2,022M, Platform Investment, 2023) at 18.5x; Apex Medical Group ($1,920M, Recapitalization, 2016, Midwest) at 17.9x. [D:MA-2023-0330, D:MA-2016-0065]
Silver Health Partners ($35M, Leveraged Buyout, 2022) at 13.8x; Granite Care ($336M, Platform Investment, 2020) at 13.6x. [D:MA-2022-0311, D:MA-2020-0408]
Hudson Medical Group ($436M, Strategic Acquisition, 2020) at 9.3x. [D:MA-2020-0496]

valuation_context.title: Upper-quartile pricing is defensible; its own median sits below that level
points: Comparable deals run 10.7x to 15.3x, median 12.8x; 75th percentile is defensible as the 16.8% margin beats the 12.9% comp median. [V:comps]
Its median paid of 13.8x is above the comparable median of 12.8x and below the 15.3x upper quartile. [V:comps, T:record]
Cost-synergy headroom of $15M-$25M supports a stretch bid; buyer revenue not researched. [V:synergy]

risk_flags.title: Size mismatch
risk_flags.concern: Only 1 of 5 deals sits in the $100M-$400M comparable size band, against a median deal of $436M.
risk_flags.mitigant: It has done a $35M deal and a $336M deal in the same sub-sector.
risk_flags.reality: Target size is within its range but not its usual pattern. [K:size_band, D:MA-2022-0311, D:MA-2020-0408]

risk_flags.title: Thin Midwest record
risk_flags.concern: Only 1 deal in the target's region, and regional history is a slight factor against.
risk_flags.mitigant: That deal, Apex Medical Group (2016), was in the Midwest; its footprint includes Illinois and Wisconsin.
risk_flags.reality: Regional evidence is limited and dated. [S:geo_fit, D:MA-2016-0065, P:2]

risk_flags.title: Price gap to sponsors
risk_flags.concern: A 75th-percentile bid of 15.3x is above its 13.8x median paid.
risk_flags.mitigant: It paid 18.5x and 17.9x in two deals, and synergy headroom is $15M-$25M.
risk_flags.reality: Stretching is possible, but buyer revenue is not researched, so capacity is unconfirmed. [V:comps, T:record, V:synergy]

conviction.rationale: Five deals in the target's own sub-sector, one in its region, and a first-place rank on the priority list drive the call; the thin Midwest record and size pattern are the offsets. [T:record, R:rank, C:conviction]
